title: Grade 10 Biology National Exam & Practice 2015 (5 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 5 chapters (100 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences explains the traditional use of biotechnology's production of:
questions.explanation:
Traditional biotechnology involves the use of natural organisms and simple techniques to produce products like yogurt, cheese, and other fermented foods at home or small-scale settings.

 The other options involve modern or industrial biotechnology.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences is correct about mitosis? It:
options: produces four different daughter cells from a single cell.
is the division of sex cells resulting in identical daughter cells.
produces half number of chromosomes from the original cell.
is the division of somatic cells to make identical daughter cells.
questions.explanation: Mitosis is the process by which somatic (body) cells divide to produce two daughter cells that are genetically identical to the parent cell and contain the full (diploid) chromosome number.

questions.questionText: A cross between pea plants having heterozygous genotype (Rr) has been made. Which of the following is correct about the offspring according to the Mendelian inheritance? The genotypic probability of getting
questions.explanation: A cross between two heterozygous pea plants (Rr × Rr) produces the following genotypes in a Punnett square: Thus, the probability of offspring being homozygous recessive (rr) is 25%.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about DNA? It is
options: smaller molecule and coding for only protein.
made of phosphate, sugar and bases.
questions.explanation:
DNA (Deoxyribonucleic acid) is a polymer made up of monomers called nucleotides.

 Each nucleotide consists of three parts: a phosphate group, a deoxyribose sugar, and a nitrogenous base (A, T, C, or G).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following monohybrid crosses can be a test cross?
questions.explanation:
A test cross is always performed by crossing an organism with an unknown genotype (usually dominant phenotype) with an organism that is homozygous recessive (rr).

 This allows a scientist to determine the genotype of the first organism.
 Among the options, RR x rr (crossing a homozygous dominant with a homozygous recessive) is a type of cross used in Mendelian genetics and fits the definition of crossing with the recessive parent (though Rr x rr is the most common test cross).

questions.questionText: In the nervous co-ordination system, which of the following statements explains the synapse? It is a:
options: part of the skull that encloses brain for the purpose of protection.
chemical that transmits nerve impulse across the nervous system.
short term change in the electrical potential on the surface of cells.
junction between two neurons or a neuron and a muscle.
questions.explanation: A synapse is the junction where a nerve impulse passes from one neuron to another neuron or from a neuron to a muscle cell, allowing communication within the nervous system.

questions.questionText: Two students want to demonstrate a simple spinal reflex action using the knee jerk reflex. One of them sits down with one leg loosely crossed over the other. The other hits the crossed leg just below the knee cap Gentle but  firmly using the edge of his hand. Which one of the following situations will happen during this demonstration? The:
options: impulse travels to quadriceps muscle from the brain.
lower leg will jerk downwards and inwards.
questions.explanation:
In the knee-jerk reflex (a simple spinal reflex), tapping the tendon below the kneecap stretches the quadriceps muscle.

 This stretch is detected by sensory neurons, which send an impulse to the spinal cord. The spinal cord immediately sends a motor impulse back to the quadriceps, causing the lower leg to jerk downwards and slightly inwards without involving the brain.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following eye structures is correctly matched with its function?
options: Iris - controls the amount of light entering the eye.
Pupil - serves as the eye's protective outer layer.
Choroid - bends the light into the eye.
Cornea - provides nutrition to the retina.
questions.explanation: The Iris contains muscles that constrict or dilate the pupil, thereby controlling the amount of light that enters the eye and reaches the retina.

questions.questionText: What is the function of dermis of the skin? It:
options: forms a waterproof around the body tissue.
contains blood vessels and sweat glands.
acts as protection against heat loss.
protects the entry of pathogens into the body.
questions.explanation: The dermis is the second layer of skin, characterized by a dense matrix of connective tissue that houses structures like blood vessels, hair follicles, and sweat glands.

questions.questionText: Children who play by spinning round and round fast, when they stop, they feel dizzy. Why?
options: The fluid in their semicircular canals keeps on moving after they stop.
The sensory hairs vibrate highly in response to movement of their body.
The otoliths round in the same direction with the head.
The optic nerves reports that the children are still moving.
questions.explanation:
Dizziness after spinning is caused by inertia affecting the endolymph fluid in the semicircular canals of the inner ear.

 When the body stops, the fluid continues to move for a moment, sending signals to the brain that the head is still rotating, leading to the sensation of dizziness.

questions.questionText: When does menstruation start in women with no obvious reproductive a health problem? It happens when
options: pregnancy occurs and the embryo obtains nourishment and oxygen.
the spongy lining of the uterus detaches in the absence of pregnancy.
the fertilized ovum reaches the uterus and attaches into the thick, spongy lining.
the FSH stimulates the development of a follicle in the ovary and the egg ripens.
questions.explanation:
Menstruation is the shedding of the thickened inner lining of the uterus (endometrium/spongy lining).

 This occurs specifically when there is no pregnancy, causing a drop in progesterone and estrogen, which triggers the detachment of the lining.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences is correctly matched with the function of kidney structures?
options: Glomerulus - concentrates urine and conserves water
Loop of Henle - involved in ultrafiltration
Bowman's capsule - acts as a filter to produce urine
Cortex - monitors the osmotic pressure of the blood
questions.explanation: The Bowman's capsule surrounds the glomerulus and collects the fluid forced out of the blood, acting as the initial filter to produce urine (filtrate).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following temperature controlling mechanisms in homotherms is categorized into behavioral method?
options: Shivering as a result of drop in temperature
Seeking shade when the temperature rises
Constriction of capillaries when the temperature falls
questions.explanation:
Behavioral mechanisms involve voluntary actions.

 Seeking shade is a voluntary action used to reduce heat gain and thus control body temperature, classifying it as a behavioral mechanism. 

The other options (A, C, D) are physiological (involuntary) responses.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT the function of the liver?
questions.explanation:
The liver functions include storing glycogen, controlling cholesterol levels, and forming bile.

 However, monosaccharide metabolism primarily occurs in the cells of the body (e.g., glycolysis in cytoplasm) rather than being a direct function of the liver.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the movement of materials in plants?
options: The transport of organic materials is due to transpiration.
Passive transport can take place in the pholem.
Active transport can take place in the xylem.
Water is transported in dead tissue.
questions.explanation:
Water is transported through the xylem vessels, which are composed of dead tissue (tracheids and vessel elements).

 Organic materials (sugars) are transported in the phloem, and their movement is active, not passive, and not primarily driven by transpiration (which drives water movement in the xylem).

questions.questionText: What will happen if an agriculture extension worker injects gibberellins into a dwarf plant? The:
questions.explanation:
Gibberellins are plant hormones that promote stem elongation and cell division.

When an agriculture extension worker injects gibberellins into a dwarf plant, the hormone stimulates stem growth, making the plant taller.

The other options (leaf fall, side shoot growth, root storage) are not primary effects of gibberellins.

questions.questionText:
A biologist collected two types of seeds (SA and SB) from the field and sowed them in moist soils enriched with nutrients. Then, he recorded his observations as follows:

 SA
     The seedling of this seed emerged from the soil curved while pushing up through the soil.

 The hypocotyl straightened and carried the cotyledons and plumule above the soil surface.

 SB
     The plumule of the seedling pushed its way out of the soil, while the cotyledon remained underground.

     Unlike what occurred during the germination of SA, the plumule of this seed did not form a hook.

Which one of the following is correct about the observations of the biologist?
options: SA is of a monocot, while SB is of a dicot.
Both SA and SB are of monocots.
SA is of a dicot, while SB is of a monocot.
Both SA and SB are of dicots.
questions.explanation:
The observations describe two types of germination:

SA shows epigeal germination (cotyledons pulled above ground by the lengthening hypocotyl hook).
 This type of germination is typical of dicots (Dicotyledons).

SB shows hypogeal germination (plumule pushes straight out while cotyledons remain underground).

 This type is typical of monocots (Monocotyledons).

Therefore, SA is of a dicot, while SB is of a monocot.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an Ethiopian endemic plant?
questions.explanation:
Noug (Guizotia abyssinica) is endemic to Ethiopia, meaning it naturally grows only in this region.

 The other plants—Bunna (coffee), Bahir zaf, and Avocado—are found in multiple regions outside Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: Walia ibex is an endemic animal species in Ethiopia which is found in
questions.explanation: The Walia Ibex (Capra walie) is an endemic and critically endangered wild goat species found almost exclusively in the Simien Mountains National Park in northern Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: All of the following sentences are correct about pollution EXCEPT
options: burning fossil fuels increases pollution due to the release of hydrocarbons.
burning of wood increases pollution by causing global dimming which blocks sunlight.
deforestation increases the amount of CO₂ absorbed from the atmosphere.
decomposition of dead bodies increases the amount of CO₂ in the atmosphere.
questions.explanation:
The statement that deforestation increases the amount of CO₂ absorbed** is INCORRECT.

 Deforestation *decreases* the absorption of CO2 (because trees are carbon sinks), leading to a net *ncrease of CO2 in the atmosphere, which contributes to pollution (global warming).

questions.questionText:
Three students designed the following experimental settings to understand the actual taste of a food.

 Student 1: Blind folded two students, one of them tightly holding the nose while the other without holding the nose and tasting the food. 

Student 2 : Blind foldeed one student and the other left with open eyes, both holding their nose tightly while tasting the food.

 Student 3: None of the participants blind folded and only one of them holding her nose tightly while tasting the food.

 Student 4: None of the participants blind folded and both of them taste the food without holding the nose.

 Which student designed the most appropriate experiment?
questions.explanation:
Student 1 controlled the effect of sight by blindfolding both participants and changed only one variable (holding the nose or not).

 This makes the experiment fair and appropriate for testing the role of smell in tasting food.

questions.questionText: Which inorganic ion is a required component for the synthesis of thyroid hormones?
questions.explanation: Iodine is incorporated into the thyroid hormones (T3 and T4), which regulate the body's metabolism.

questions.questionText: What happens if the axon is stimulated? Formation of
options: positive charge outside of the axon
negative charge in both sides of the axon
questions.explanation: When an axon is stimulated, Na+ channels open and Na+ ions rush in, causing depolarization where the interior of the axon becomes briefly positive.

questions.questionText: What is the maximum number of trophic levels that a stable ecosystem typically supports?
questions.explanation: Due to the massive energy loss (90 percent) at each transfer, the energy available for higher trophic levels quickly becomes insufficient, limiting most ecosystems to about three to five trophic levels.

questions.questionText: Which part of the stem, found in the vascular bundle of dicots, is responsible for the radial expansion of the stem?
questions.explanation: The cambium is the meristematic layer that divides to form secondary xylem and phloem, resulting in the thickening (radial expansion) of the stem.

questions.questionText: Short sightedness is corrected by a concave lens because the problem arises due to a
options: weak eye lens that converges light slightly.
powerful eye lens that diverges light.
weak eye lens that diverges light.
strong eye lens that converges light too soon.
questions.explanation:
Short sightedness (myopia) occurs when the lens is too strong (or the eyeball is too long), causing light to be focused in front of the retina.

 A concave (diverging) lens is needed to push the focal point back.

questions.questionText: In the chloroplast, the stroma is the site where which set of photosynthetic reactions occurs?
questions.explanation: The stroma, the fluid-filled space surrounding the grana, is where the light-independent reactions (dark reactions/Calvin cycle) take place.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an applied field of biology?
questions.explanation: Pharmacology uses biological knowledge to develop drugs and treatments, making it an applied field. The others are pure, fundamental fields.

questions.questionText: The famous experiment that disproved the theory of spontaneous generation and contributed to germ theory was performed by:
questions.explanation: Louis Pasteur is renowned for his work that disproved spontaneous generation and established the science of fermentation and pasteurization.

questions.questionText: The discovery of DNA's structure fundamentally revolutionized which two fields of biology, as seen in the text?
questions.explanation: DNA is the subject of Molecular Biology, and its structure provided the basis for modern Genetics, which deals with heredity and variation.

questions.questionText: Which branch studies the external form and structure of an organism, such as its shape and visible features?
questions.explanation: Morphology is the study of external form and structure.

questions.questionText: The development of Penicillin, a significant biological discovery in medicine, is credited to:
questions.explanation: Penicillin is mentioned as a major biological discovery contributing to society. Although Alexander Fleming is not explicitly named as the discoverer in the provided text, his discovery of penicillin is the most accurate answer for this historical achievement.

questions.questionText: A biologist investigating the structure and development of the gastrula stage of an embryo is focused on the early formation of:
questions.explanation: The gastrula stage is described as the stage after blastula during which the embryo develops two layers.

questions.questionText: In a dicot seed, the main food storage tissue that nourishes the embryo is typically the:
questions.explanation: Dicot seeds typically have two fleshy cotyledons that store food materials, as the endosperm is usually absent or greatly reduced by the time the seed matures.

questions.questionText: The formation of Oxyhaemoglobin (haemoglobin with oxygen) during oxygen transport in the body is a chemical change, linking this biological process to:
questions.explanation: The transportation of Oxygen in the body involves the formation of Oxyhaemoglobin. This and all metabolic pathways are chemical changes, necessitating knowledge of Chemistry.

questions.questionText: What type of lipid functions primarily as a component of cell membranes and an emulsifier?
questions.explanation: Phospholipids are the structural components of cell membranes and their amphipathic nature allows them to act as emulsifiers.

questions.questionText: Which two sciences are essential to understanding the movement of water from the root to the leaves of a plant due to cohesion and capillary action?
questions.explanation: Water conduction involves Physics (cohesion/capillary action) and Chemistry (molecular structure of water).

questions.questionText: Louis Pasteur's work contributed to solving major biological problems in all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Watson and Crick discovered the structure of DNA, not Louis Pasteur. Pasteur's work includes fermentation, pasteurization, and early vaccines.

questions.questionText: The largest and most diverse group of plants, characterized by the presence of true flowers and the production of seeds enclosed within a fruit, is the:
questions.explanation: Angiosperms, or flowering plants, are the most diverse group and are characterized by the production of flowers and seeds enclosed within fruits (covered seeds).

questions.questionText: What is the key difference that distinguishes a saturated fatty acid from an unsaturated fatty acid?
options: Saturated fats are liquid at room temperature.
Saturated fats have at least one Carbon=Carbon double bond.
Saturated fats have only single Carbon-Carbon bonds (are saturated with hydrogen).
Unsaturated fats are used for insulation.
questions.explanation: Saturated fatty acids lack Carbon=Carbon double bonds, making their chains straight and allowing them to pack tightly, typically resulting in a solid fat at room temperature.

questions.questionText: The male reproductive structure in a flower that produces pollen grains is the:
questions.explanation: The stamen is the male organ, and its part, the anther, produces the pollen grains which contain the male gametes.

questions.questionText: The organelle in plant cells that is the site of photosynthesis and contains the pigment chlorophyll is the:
questions.explanation: The chloroplast is the photosynthetic apparatus in plant cells, and it contains chlorophyll, the green pigment necessary to capture light energy.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements correctly describes chromosome structure?
options: pair of chromosomes is heteroygous in nature.
Chromosomes are similar to a gene in structure.
The DNA is wrapped with ribose sugar to form a chromosome.
Chromosomes are made up of histone bounded DNA.
questions.explanation:
A chromosome is the highest level of organization of genetic material. 
It is composed of a very long molecule of DNA that is tightly coiled and packaged around specialized proteins called histones.
 This complex of DNA and protein is called chromatin.

 Therefore, the statement that Chromosomes are made up of histone bounded DNA is the most accurate description of their composition.

questions.questionText: Pollination is defined as the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma. Which of the following is NOT a common agent for this transfer?
questions.explanation: The main agents of pollination are wind, insects, water, and sometimes birds or bats. Gravity can play a minor role in certain plants, but it is not considered a primary *agent* of transfer like the others.

questions.questionText: Which element must an amino acid contain that is not found in pure carbohydrates or lipids?
questions.explanation: Amino acids (and thus proteins) contain an Amino group (NH2), which incorporates Nitrogen (N). Lipids and pure carbohydrates lack this element.

questions.questionText: The first incubation period of HIV is characterized by a duration of
options: 2-3 years for the progress of infection to AIDS.
3-12 weeks when mild symptoms are manifested.
20 years before all the symptoms appear in well-nourished people.
questions.explanation: The first incubation period (acute HIV infection) typically occurs 3-12 weeks after exposure and is often accompanied by flu-like symptoms.

questions.questionText: The study of bacteria is known as:
questions.explanation: Bacteriology is the specific sub-discipline of Microbiology defined as the study of bacteria.

questions.questionText: Studying how an organism forms identical copies of itself (multiplies) is a concern of which major category of biological branches?
questions.explanation: Many other branches of biology are concerned with the various life processes, such as how an organism multiplies or forms identical copies of itself.

questions.questionText: The bond formed between two monosaccharides is called a:
questions.explanation: A Glycosidic bond links two sugar units together to form a disaccharide or polysaccharide.

questions.questionText: What mechanism was used by Gregor Mendel to protect the garden peas from self-pollination? He
options: opened the flower bud before pollen matured.
sterilized the male part of the flower using chemicals.
covered the flower and protects it from pollinating agents.
selected pure dominant traits for breeding.
questions.explanation:
Mendel performed cross-pollination experiments on pea plants. 

To prevent the flowers from self-pollinating and to ensure he controlled which pollen fertilized which flower, he first castrated the flower (removed the stamens, the male parts) and then covered the flower and protects it from pollinating agents (like insects or wind) using bags or nets until he was ready to brush on pollen from a different parent plant.

questions.questionText: Which trophic level usually has the greatest number of individual organisms in a Pyramid of Number for a typical forest ecosystem?
questions.explanation: In a typical upright Pyramid of Number, the Producers (T1) form the base and have the largest number of individual organisms (e.g., millions of grass blades or leaves).

questions.questionText: Bushing of a plant results from
options: increased production of auxin by the main shoot.
decreased production of auxin by side shoots.
removal of the inhibitory effect of auxin.
cancellation of the positive effect of apical dominance.
questions.explanation: Bushing (lateral growth) occurs when the apical bud is removed, which removes the inhibitory effect of auxin (apical dominance) and allows the lateral buds to grow.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following systems is responsible for protecting the body from infection?
questions.explanation: The primary role of the immune system is to detect, neutralize, and defend the body against foreign pathogens such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites.

questions.questionText: Excessive production of dilute urine can be a symptom of a deficiency in which hormone?
questions.explanation: A lack of ADH (or kidney insensitivity to it) prevents water from being reabsorbed, leading to excessive urination (a condition called diabetes insipidus).

questions.questionText: The exchange of gases and nutrients across the placenta occurs through the process of:
options: Diffusion (and active transport for some substances)
questions.explanation: Oxygen, carbon dioxide, glucose, and wastes move across the placental barrier primarily by diffusion due to concentration gradients.

questions.questionText: What is the primary mechanism by which carbon is removed from the atmosphere and converted into organic compounds?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process by which producers (plants and algae) use carbon dioxide from the atmosphere to synthesize glucose (organic carbon compounds), thus fixing atmospheric carbon.

questions.questionText: The branch of biology studying the 'texture of leaves' and the 'shape of the stem' is:
questions.explanation: Morphology is the study of external form and structure, with the shape and texture of leaves/stem given as examples of structures studied.

questions.questionText: Which of the following conditions is NOT typically required for a viable seed to successfully germinate?
questions.explanation: Viable seeds need water, oxygen, and an appropriate temperature to germinate. Light is generally not required and can sometimes be inhibitory.

questions.questionText: An allergy is an inappropriate and excessive immune response to a normally harmless substance called an:
questions.explanation: Allergens trigger the release of histamine from mast cells, leading to symptoms like swelling and itching.

questions.questionText: Which of the following processes requires the least dependence on the principles of Physics for its explanation?
options: Molecular transport across the cell membrane
questions.explanation: The electron transport chain, a redox reaction involving electron transfer and transport, is fundamentally explained by Chemistry. Water transport and capillary action in plants are based on physical properties of liquids.

questions.questionText: The disease Diabetes Mellitus is caused by a deficiency in or a lack of response to:
questions.explanation: Diabetes involves high blood sugar due to problems with insulin production (Type 1) or cell response (Type 2).

questions.questionText: The primary role of white blood cells (leukocytes) is:
options: To produce ATP for the body
To defend the body against pathogens and foreign substances
questions.explanation: White blood cells are the mobile units of the immune system.

questions.questionText: Which major discovery is a direct application of the theory of evolution, explaining the diversity of finch beaks in the Galapagos Islands?
questions.explanation: The beaks of Darwin's finches are listed as an example of the subject studied under the branch of Evolution.

questions.questionText: The long, coiled tube attached to the testes where sperm mature and are stored is the:
questions.explanation: The epididymis is necessary for sperm to gain motility and the ability to fertilize an egg.

questions.questionText: What is the collective term for the protective membranes (dura mater, arachnoid mater, pia mater) that cover the brain and spinal cord?
questions.explanation: The meninges protect the delicate tissues of the CNS.

questions.questionText: The structure of the palisade mesophyll with its compactly arranged, elongated cells and numerous chloroplasts is an adaptation for:
questions.explanation: The palisade mesophyll cells are situated at the top of the leaf to maximize their exposure to sunlight and their photosynthetic capacity.

questions.questionText: A biologist is examining the detailed structure of the Parenchyma and connective tissue using a microscope. Which branch of biology is this person specializing in?
questions.explanation: Histology is the study of the details of tissue structure, with parenchyma and connective tissue given as examples of structures studied.

questions.questionText: In the process of pollination, the transfer of pollen within the same flower or to another flower on the same plant is known as:
questions.explanation: Self-pollination (autogamy) is the transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma of the same flower or a different flower on the same plant.

questions.questionText: What is the primary function of an antibody?
options: To specifically bind to antigens and mark them for destruction
questions.explanation: Antibodies are Y-shaped proteins that tag foreign invaders (antigens) for destruction by other immune cells.

questions.questionText: Which of the following factors has a direct and significant effect on the rate of photosynthesis, as it is a necessary raw material for the Calvin cycle (dark reaction)?
options: Mineral nutrient levels in the soil
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is one of the two raw materials for photosynthesis. Its concentration is a limiting factor, as it is fixed into glucose during the light-independent reactions.

questions.questionText: Breakdown of the thick spongy wall of the uterus at the end of the menstrual cycle is associated with the
options: increase in oestrogen and progesterone concentration.
decrease in progesterone and estrogen concentration.
questions.explanation:
Menstruation is triggered by the decrease in progesterone and estrogen concentration when the corpus luteum degenerates.

 This drop signals the uterine lining to break down.

questions.questionText: The protein molecules that attach to DNA and help organize and condense the chromatin are called:
questions.explanation: Histones are the core proteins around which DNA wraps to form nucleosomes, the basic unit of chromatin.

questions.questionText: The paired homologous chromosomes in Prophase I are referred to as a:
questions.explanation: A bivalent or tetrad consists of one homologous pair, comprising four sister chromatids.

questions.questionText: Which human activity is contributing most significantly to the imbalance in the global carbon cycle?
options: The use of chemical fertilizers in agriculture.
The combustion of wood and coal for energy.
The conversion of nitrogen gas into nitrates.
questions.explanation: The combustion of fossil fuels (coal, oil, gas) for industry, power, and transport releases enormous amounts of stored carbon into the atmosphere as CO2, exceeding the capacity of natural sinks to absorb it.

questions.questionText: What separates during Anaphase I of meiosis?
questions.explanation: Anaphase I separates the homologous chromosomes, moving the maternal and paternal chromosomes to opposite poles.

questions.questionText: Which of the following food items would provide the most unsaturated fatty acids?
questions.explanation: Olive oil (and most liquid plant oils) are rich in unsaturated fatty acids, which have kinks that prevent close packing, keeping them liquid at room temperature.

questions.questionText: During the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis, light energy is primarily converted into which forms of chemical energy?
questions.explanation: The light reactions capture light energy and convert it into the high-energy intermediate molecules, Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP) and Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide Phosphate (NADPH).

questions.questionText: The movement of water from the roots up to the top leaves of tall trees is carried out by
options: active transport in both the roots and leaves.
the low cohesive and adhesive forces of water in the xylem.
active transport in the roots and osmosis in the leaves.
loss of water by transpiration and its replacement by osmosis.
questions.explanation: The main mechanism is the transpiration pull: the loss of water by transpiration from leaves creates a negative pressure (tension) that draws water up the xylem, which is then replaced by water from the roots via osmosis.

questions.questionText: Which group of microscopic organisms is studied under Microbiology along with bacteria and viruses?
questions.explanation: Microbiology includes the study of bacteria, archaea, protists, viruses, microscopic algae, and fungi.

questions.questionText: If a cell fails to pass a checkpoint, it may enter a non-dividing state known as the:
questions.explanation: The G0 phase is a resting state where the cell is metabolically active but no longer preparing to divide.

questions.questionText: Who is considered the 'Father of Genetics' for formulating the fundamental laws of heredity through his work with pea plants?
questions.explanation: Gregor Mendel's work on heredity and variation, resulting in his laws of inheritance, established him as the father of Genetics.

questions.questionText: What is the primary storage polysaccharide found in animal liver and muscle cells?
questions.explanation: Glycogen is the compact, branched polymer used by animals to store excess glucose.

questions.questionText: The process where necessary substances like glucose, amino acids, and water are selectively moved back from the renal tubules into the blood is called:
questions.explanation: Tubular reabsorption is a vital process to retain valuable molecules and water, preventing them from being lost in the urine.

questions.questionText: What is the primary function of Sodium ions (Na+) and Potassium ions (K+) in the nervous system?
options: To form the structural myelin sheath.
To establish the electrochemical gradient necessary for nerve impulse transmission.
To dissolve oxygen in the blood.
questions.explanation: The movement of Na+ and K+ across the neuron membrane generates the action potentials (nerve impulses).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is considered the first line of defense in the human immune system?
questions.explanation: The skin and mucous membranes act as physical barriers, preventing pathogens from entering the body.

questions.questionText: The crop varieties developed by Professor Gebissa Ejeta were specifically resistant to which parasitic threat?
questions.explanation: His Sorghum varieties were resistant to drought and the parasitic weed Striga (witchweed).

questions.questionText: In a plant leaf, the lower epidermis typically has more stomata than the upper epidermis. This adaptation is primarily to:
questions.explanation: Placing stomata on the lower surface reduces direct exposure to sunlight, minimizing water loss while still allowing sufficient CO2 intake.

questions.questionText: Professor Gebissa Ejeta's contribution primarily provided a solution for farmers facing which two environmental challenges in crop production?
questions.explanation: His Sorghum varieties were resistant to drought and the parasitic weed Striga (witchweed).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a key application that arose from discoveries in the field of Genetics?
questions.explanation: Genetic Engineering is a major applied field that directly uses the principles of heredity and variation established by the pure field of Genetics.

questions.questionText: The phosphorus cycle differs from the carbon and nitrogen cycles because it:
options: Requires energy from sunlight to function.
Is primarily an exchange of gases with the atmosphere.
Involves the weathering of rocks as its main source.
questions.explanation: The Phosphorus cycle is mainly geological. Its primary reservoir and source of new phosphorus is the weathering of rocks, which releases phosphate ions into the soil and water.

questions.questionText: Which phase of mitosis is essentially the reverse of prophase, involving the reformation of the nuclear envelope?
questions.explanation: In telophase, the nuclear envelope and nucleoli reform, and chromosomes decondense back into chromatin.

questions.questionText: In which molecule are Phosphate ions (PO4 3-) most essential for the transfer of energy?
questions.explanation: ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) stores energy in the bonds between its three phosphate groups, which is released when one phosphate group is cleaved off.

questions.questionText: Passive immunity, such as the temporary protection gained from a mother to a baby through breastfeeding, is characterized by:
questions.explanation: Passive immunity is short-lived because the body does not create its own memory cells, it just uses the transferred antibodies.

questions.questionText: Robert Koch is famous for formulating a set of criteria used to determine:
options: The structure of the DNA molecule
The microbial cause of a specific disease
questions.explanation: Robert Koch established the microbial cause of specific diseases using what is now known as Koch's postulates.

questions.questionText: Two species of birds attempting to use the same limited nesting sites in a forest illustrates which type of ecological interaction?
questions.explanation: Since the competition is between two different species (two species of birds) for a limited resource (nesting sites), it is defined as interspecific competition.

questions.questionText: When an animal excretes waste or dies, phosphorus is returned to the soil or water primarily through the action of:
questions.explanation: Decomposers (bacteria and fungi) break down the organic compounds in dead matter and waste, releasing the phosphorus back into the soil as inorganic phosphate ions in a process called decomposition or mineralization.

questions.questionText: What is the key advantage of sexual reproduction over asexual reproduction?
questions.explanation: The variation from meiosis and fertilization allows populations to adapt better to changing environments.

questions.questionText: A cell that possesses two sets of chromosomes (one from each parent) is described as:
questions.explanation: Diploid cells have two homologous copies of each chromosome, characteristic of somatic cells.

questions.questionText: The cell cycle is divided into two main parts: Interphase and what other phase?
questions.explanation: The cell cycle consists of Interphase (G1, S, G2) and the Mitotic (M) phase, which includes mitosis and cytokinesis.

questions.questionText: Which type of protein is responsible for fighting infections by recognizing and neutralizing foreign bodies?
questions.explanation: Antibodies, or Immunoglobulins, are highly specific defense proteins that bind to antigens on pathogens.
